title: Proof-space pilot contract
intro: The pilot of goal G9: a fresh receiver gathers, from content roots and its own configuration only, every object one Sigma receipt needs, checks their bytes, and only then replays the receipt under a verification profile it admits. This contract fixes the terms. The resolution layer (PS-02, PS-03, PS-04) is implemented in `warrant/pilot.py` and tested by `tests/pilot_test.py` (A1-A12, D1-D10, F1-F4, K1-K2); the replay itself and everything after it are deferred to the cards named below.

Scope: the pilot is not part of SPEC.md. It adds no Warrant record type and no engine rule, `engine.assess` does not read it, and the Sigma receipt keeps SPEC §7's members and the meaning of `lost`. A rule below is enforced (cases of `tests/pilot_test.py` that pass, and mutants of `tests/mutants.py` that make them fail), deferred to a filed G9 obligation, or excluded from the pilot.

rows.rule: The pilot's one proof kind is SPEC §7's `sigma-resume` receipt, unchanged: its dependency fields are read only through `compute.receipt_problem`, so a receipt with another member, a missing one or a malformed hash is refused.

The predicate verified: under an admitted profile p, receipt r is VERIFIED iff SPEC §7's admission holds with p's provider and runtime: target accepted, `lost` empty, `(input, environment)` equal to the condition's, and the receiver's own replay from the root gives NORMAL_FORM with result equal to `claimed` and to the condition's `expect`. A paused, blocked or unavailable replay is not VERIFIED.
Cycle blobs (`impossible` items) and any second proof kind are outside the pilot; no other kind inherits its labels.
rows.excluded: a second proof kind is the proposal card PS-14, not filed

sections.title: Typed addresses and object stores
text: A typed address is `<kind>:<hex64>`; the hex64 is the SHA-256 of the object's exact bytes (SPEC §2). The pilot's kinds, each with the tag checked on its bytes and the dependency fields read after it:

rows.rule: Anything but `<kind>:<64 lowercase hex digits>` (`shapes.hex64`) is BAD_ADDRESS, refused before any path is built or any store read: path traversal at the right length, uppercase, a trailing newline.

An object whose bytes hash to its address but lack its kind's tag is KIND_MISMATCH, refused before its dependency fields are read. JSON kinds are canonical bytes (`jcs.loads`): other bytes are refused, never normalized, whatever the parser raises on them.
A record id is no object address (a store's `records/` is never read), and a record envelope named by its digest is not an object of any pilot kind.

The receiver consults its configured local stores in order: layout `blobs` (`<dir>/<hex64>`, a Warrant store's `blobs/`) and layout `fanout` (`<dir>/<2 hex>/<62 hex>`, a warrant-agent object store). Only a regular file reached from the store's directory without a symlink is an object of that store: each component is opened relative to its parent without following one, so a symlink, a directory swapped for a symlink between check and use, a FIFO (opened without blocking) or a directory is not.
One typed address resolves to the same bytes and the same closure id through either store, both, or stores that each hold part of the closure; the closure manifest names no store.

Bytes a store holds under a name that do not hash to it are DIGEST_MISMATCH naming that store, refused before any kind reads them; no other store is consulted past them. The digest is checked on the whole file as read to its end, also when it grew after its size was taken.
Nothing is fetched from outside the configured stores: no network, no store an object names.
rows.excluded: a network resolver is the proposal card PS-12, not filed; `warrant/pilot.py` opens only files of configured stores

sections.title: The closure before verification
text: The closure of a root is every object reachable through the dependency fields of the table above, walked depth first. Every dependency field is required; the pilot has no optional one.

rows.rule: Every dependency field of the kinds table is followed: a receipt's `input`, `environment`, `checkpoint` and `state`, an environment's `hashes`, a root's `requires`. A missing object anywhere in the closure is MISSING at its address. `claimed` is a result hash, not a dependency.

Verification starts only on RESOLVED: `Receiver.check` calls the verifier once with the whole closure, and on any other result never calls it and answers the resolution. A result other than RESOLVED carries no object.
A shared dependency is read once; every reference followed counts toward `pilot_edges`, repeats included, so repeated references do not escape the aggregate limit.
An address met again on its own reference path is CYCLE. SHA-256 addresses cannot form a cycle; the guard is shown on a stand-in fetch, and a diamond is not a cycle.
Dependency fields are read with the kind's exact shape: a receipt or root with another member, an environment out of order, a root naming an address twice or nothing is MALFORMED.
A kind the receiver does not admit is UNKNOWN_KIND, at the root or as a dependency, also a kind `warrant/pilot.py` knows.

sections.title: Resource bounds
text: The receiver's limits (`warrant.limits.resolve` over these defaults; a receiver sets each one in its configuration):

rows.rule: Within every limit a closure resolves as without limits; beyond one the result is LIMIT with `limit`, `value` and `bound`, and no object. Objects and bytes are admitted before an object is read, and the bytes again as read (a file grown after its size was taken); `pilot_depth` bounds the longest chain of references from the root whatever the order of the walk.

sections.title: Result meanings
text: RESOLVED establishes that every object of the closure is present in a configured store and is what its address says: byte identity under the address scheme, nothing about the objects' truth, signatures or authority, or the computation's result. INCONCLUSIVE means this receiver could not decide; REFUSED that the objects as presented are not admissible. Neither refutes a proof.

rows.rule: Each code has the one result of the table: a missing object, an unadmitted kind and an exhausted limit are INCONCLUSIVE; a bad address, a digest or kind mismatch, a malformed object and a cycle are REFUSED.
The results of verification itself (VERIFIED, and an unsupported profile or an unavailable operand never becoming VERIFIED) and their independence from duties, grants and acceptances.
A verified result grants no Warrant authority or permission: use is the receiver's own policy, view and freshness basis.

sections.title: Verification profiles
text: A profile is canonical JSON `{schema: "warrant-pilot/profile@1", rule, runtime, verifier: {entry, boot, protocol, provider, modules}, axioms, assumptions}`. `boot` is the digest of the boot script that runs the provider (`compute.BOOT`), `modules` the digest of each provider module, `provider` the identity those digests give (`compute.identity_of_files`). Pinned bytes appear only as digests; host conditions only as text in `assumptions`.

rows.rule: A profile's id is the SHA-256 of its canonical bytes, which is its `pilot-profile` address; the receiver recomputes it from the bytes it resolved. `pilot.profile` builds one from the receiver's own installed provider.

Changing any declared semantic operand alone (entry, boot, protocol, a module digest, rule, runtime, an axiom, an assumption) gives a valid profile with another id; the old profile stays separately addressable.

A profile with a member missing or added (an unpinned URL), a pin that is not a hex64 digest (a path, URL, ref, uppercase), a provider other than its module digests give, or axioms and assumptions that are not non-empty sorted lists of distinct strings is MALFORMED.

The execution-profile assumptions of the pilot's replay are declared, not pinned: the provider runs as its captured module bytes in a separate CPython interpreter (`-I -B`), which is not an OS sandbox, and a host limit or timeout is inconclusive. `pilot.profile` declares them (`pilot.ASSUMPTIONS`).
Which profiles a receiver admits, and the check that the installed provider is the one an admitted profile pins before a replay runs.

Only the receiver's configuration (`Receiver`, `Receiver.from_config`: `warrant-pilot/receiver@1`) chooses the stores, the admitted kinds and the limits; a configuration with anything else (another member, limits that are not a mapping, a layout that is not a layout name) is refused as a ValueError before it is used, and no object can add a store, kind or limit.
Fetched verifier code is never executed: the pilot runs only the receiver's installed provider (`compute.Provider`).
rows.excluded: running fetched code is the proposal card PS-13, not filed

rows.rule: A portable bundle of root descriptors and the data and verifier-description closure, verified offline without the producer's checkout or store.
Only a candidate that passes the admitted verifier is exposed as a verified result root of a continuation recipe.
Two fresh receiver processes with different client entry points verify a frozen bundle and resume its recipe to the expected root.
A retention root keeps every required reachable object through collection until it expires or is released; a lost unretained object is named unavailability.
The pilot's evidence maps each admission, integrity, closure, replay and use boundary to a negative vector lost under a named mutation, with no empty, skipped or crashed case credited.

sections.title: Trusted assumptions
text: - SHA-256 is collision resistant for every address a closure names.
- The receiver's configuration and its installed provider are the receiver's own; nothing a store or an object says changes them.
- A local store may be damaged or changed under the receiver: the digest check detects it at read time and prevents nothing; the pilot keeps no copy (retention is PS-11).
- The process boundary of the provider is not an OS sandbox (SPEC §7).
